p.i: flagitarent, vt vniuersæ huius disciplinæ corpus suis tum præceptis, tum explicationibus atque exemplis adornatum priuatis prælectionibus proponerem, equidem laudatissimæ eorum vo-luntati morem gerens, diligentiâ quàta per ua-letudine & occupationes poteram, operas meas logicas recognoui, & artis methodum τῆς Διέξο-δου περὶ μακρὸν διδασκαλίας λόγον (illud enim pro iudicii maturitate desiderabant) integram illis, vt spero, tandè exhibuit: indepostea ad præ-lum hæc descripta, si quid vtilitatis in publicum afferunt, eius non exigua pars amicis meis Vn-garis, qui sua in audiendo tum auiditate, tum constantia studium atque industriam meam excitarunt, feretur accepta.

main_text.p: Atque hæc quidem mea narratio eo spectat, vt lectores intelligant, editionem hanc temere præcipitatam non fuisse, quin potius grauissimâ illam Ludouici Viuis admonitionem, quæ extat sub finem libri quinti de tradendis disciplinis, si non per omnia obseruatam (neq; enim id mihi arrogo) saltem diligenter, soliciteque expen-sam animo fuisse; Qui non præsentib. tantum, nec eis, quibus cum viuit, prodesse volet, verum absentibus quoq; & posteris sensa animi sui monumentis literarum ad posteros confignās, principio noscat se, & vires suas expendat, quib. polleat rebus,

page.notes: Lines running in the body are the printed text of one page; the Greek phrase "τῆς Διέξοδου περὶ μακρὸν διδασκαλίας λόγον" is a doubtful transcription of a damaged Greek passage and should be checked. Several words are damaged by the scan and are uncertain. The "„" marks at the left of the last lines are printed quotation openers. The final line of the text is partly unclear and some letters are doubtful.
